title: Target evaluation for the fibrewise arrow category of a cocartesian fibration
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functor simplicial sets, mapping spaces and degreewise pullbacks of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and their coherent classification of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]. Work in containing universes for all categories and their classifications. Let $p:E\to B$ be a cocartesian fibration of quasicategories. Let $c:B\to\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)$ send each simplex to its constant arrow, and put
$$A_p=B\times_{c,\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B),\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,p)}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,E).$$
Write $s,t:A_p\to E$ for source and target evaluation. Then $A_p\to B$ is a cocartesian fibration, classified by $b\mapsto\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,E_b)$ with transport applying the transport functor of $p$ to arrows. Target evaluation $t:A_p\to E$ is also a cocartesian fibration. Its fibre at $x\in E_b$ is the target-fixed arrow category $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,E_b)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,E_b}\{x\}$, with source projection to $E_b$.

For an edge $u:x\to y$ in $E$ over $h:b\to b'$, choose a $p$-cocartesian lift $x\to h_!x$ and its factorization $u\simeq\bar u\circ(x\to h_!x)$ with $\bar u:h_!x\to y$ in $E_{b'}$. Transport for $t$ sends $a:z\to x$ in $E_b$ to $\bar u\circ h_!(a):h_!z\to y$ in $E_{b'}$. The map
$$(t,s):A_p\longrightarrow E\times_B E,$$
where the latter projects to its first factor, preserves cocartesian edges over $E$. These fibre, transport and source-projection comparisons are coherent on arbitrary simplicial parameters, with composition and identity simplices retained. They are natural under base change in $B$ and under functors of cocartesian fibrations preserving cocartesian edges. No colimits in the fibres of $p$ are assumed.

source.place: Shah, Parametrized higher category theory, Notation 4.29 (printed p.34), Definition 7.6, Proposition 7.7 and Remark 7.4 (printed pp.49-50), applied to the identity S-functor. Source-projection and transport formulas are the agent expansion of the free S-cocartesian fibration. Read online; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical assertion.

proof.text: Because $p$ is a cocartesian fibration, it is an inner fibration and, by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-equivalence-lift], an isofibration. By [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation] applied to the degreewise injection $\varnothing\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$, $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,p):\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)$ is an isofibration of quasicategories. Hence its degreewise pullback $A_p\to B$ along $c$ is an inner fibration over the quasicategory $B$, so $A_p$ is a quasicategory, and by [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-limit] the defining square is a pullback of infinity categories. Applied instead to $\{1\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$, the same lemma makes the corner map $\kappa:\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,E)\to E\times_{B,\operatorname{ev}_1}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)$ an isofibration. Since $\operatorname{ev}_1\circ c=\mathrm{id}_B$, the degreewise pullback of $\kappa$ along $(\mathrm{id}_E,c\circ p):E\to E\times_B\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)$ is exactly $t:A_p\to E$ (an $n$-simplex of either is a simplex $y$ of $E$ with a simplex of $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,E)$ over the constant arrow at $p(y)$ with target $y$). So $t$ is an inner fibration between quasicategories.

source.place: Definition 7.6 and Proposition 7.7, construction of the relative arrow object.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] with $K=\Delta^1$ (its hypotheses hold: $p$ is an inner fibration with cocartesian lifts, and the horn-cocartesian edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] satisfy its mapping-space condition by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]). Then $p_{\Delta^1}=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,p)$ is a cocartesian fibration whose cocartesian edges are exactly those with $p$-cocartesian components at both vertices, and its fibre over the constant diagram at $b$ is $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,E_b)$. The projection $A_p\to B$ is the degreewise pullback of $p_{\Delta^1}$ along $c$; a $\Lambda^n_0$-lifting problem for it whose first edge maps to a $p_{\Delta^1}$-cocartesian edge is solved by solving the image problem for $p_{\Delta^1}$ and pairing the filler with the given simplex of $B$, and a cocartesian lift of $c(h)$ from an object of $A_p$ is a lift of $h$ in $A_p$. Hence $A_p\to B$ is a cocartesian fibration, its fibre at $b$ is $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,E_b)$, and the cocartesian lift over $h:b\to b'$ of an arrow $a:z\to x$ of $E_b$ is a square $\lambda_a:a\to h_!(a)$ with $p$-cocartesian components $\chi_z:z\to h_!z$ and $\chi_x:x\to h_!x$. By [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] its straightening has value $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,E_b)$ at $b$ and transport $h_!$ applied to arrows, and the base-change clause of that lemma identifies this classification with $p$'s on all simplices of $B$.

source.place: Definition 7.6 and Proposition 7.7, fibrewise classification of the free S-cocartesian fibration.

proof.text: At a vertex b of B, the pullback condition forces the image of an arrow in Fun(Delta^1,E) to be the constant arrow at b. Thus both endpoints lie in E_b, and taking the fibre of A_p -> B gives Fun(Delta^1,E_b). For x in E_b, the fibre of t over x is obtained by imposing ev_1=x, namely Fun(Delta^1,E_b) x_{ev_1,E_b} {x}; the remaining projection is ev_0, which is s.

Let $u:x\to y$ lie over $h:b\to b'$ and choose a $p$-cocartesian edge $\chi_x:x\to h_!x$ over $h$. By [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] the mapping-space square of $\chi_x$ at the test object $y$ is a homotopy pullback; the fibre of $\operatorname{Map}_E(h_!x,y)\to\operatorname{Map}_B(b',b')$ over $\mathrm{id}_{b'}$ is $\operatorname{Map}_{E_{b'}}(h_!x,y)$ by [lem-coef-infinity-edge-pullback-mapping-fiber] ($K=\Delta^0$, degenerate edge), so $u$ has a factorization $u\simeq\bar u\circ\chi_x$ with $\bar u:h_!x\to y$ in $E_{b'}$, unique up to contractible choice. For $a:z\to x$ in $E_b$ take the square $\lambda_a:a\to h_!(a)$ of step 2 and compose it in $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,E)$ with the square $h_!(a)\to\bar u\circ h_!(a)$ whose source component is $\mathrm{id}_{h_!z}$ and target component $\bar u$ (an edge of $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,E_{b'})$). The composite $\sigma:a\to\bar u\circ h_!(a)$ lies over the constant square at $h$, so it is an edge of $A_p$ over $h$; its source component is $\chi_z$ and its target component is $\bar u\chi_x\simeq u$; adjusting by this equivalence inside the target fibre (an inner horn filling in $E$ over the degenerate edge) gives an edge with $t(\sigma)=u$.

source.place: Proposition 7.7 and Remark 7.4, cocartesian factorization and arrow-square mapping spaces.

proof.text: We show that $\sigma$ is $t$-cocartesian; by step 1 $t$ is an inner fibration, so by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] it suffices that for each object $c:w\to v$ of $A_p$, lying over the constant arrow at some $b''$, the square with rows $\operatorname{Map}_{A_p}(a',c)\to\operatorname{Map}_{A_p}(a,c)$ (precomposition with $\sigma$, where $a'=\bar u h_!(a)$) and $\operatorname{Map}_E(y,v)\to\operatorname{Map}_E(x,v)$ (precomposition with $u$) is a homotopy pullback. (i) Right-pinched mapping spaces are defined degreewise by sets of maps $\Delta^{n+1}\to-$, so $\operatorname{Map}_{A_p}(a,c)=\operatorname{Map}_B(b,b'')\times_{\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Arr}B}(cb,cb'')}\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Arr}E}(a,c)$ strictly. By [lem-coef-infinity-edge-pullback-mapping-fiber](3) with $K=\Delta^1$, the right map is a Kan fibration of Kan complexes, so this strict pullback is a homotopy pullback; by [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-morphism-square] for the identity arrows of $B$, $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Arr}B}(cb,cb'')\simeq\operatorname{Map}_B(b,b'')\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_B(b,b'')}\operatorname{Map}_B(b,b'')$ and $c$ induces an equivalence onto it. Hence $\operatorname{Map}_{A_p}(a,c)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Arr}E}(a,c)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_E(z,w)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_E(z,v)}\operatorname{Map}_E(x,v)$ is an equivalence, naturally, with $t$ the projection to $\operatorname{Map}_E(x,v)$ (arrow-morphism-square, endpoint compatibility). (ii) By [lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting], the required square is a homotopy pullback iff, for every $f:y\to v$, precomposition with $\chi_z$ induces an equivalence $\operatorname{hofib}_{f\bar u h_!(a)}(c_*:\operatorname{Map}_E(h_!z,w)\to\operatorname{Map}_E(h_!z,v))\to\operatorname{hofib}_{fua}(c_*:\operatorname{Map}_E(z,w)\to\operatorname{Map}_E(z,v))$, using $fua\simeq f\bar u h_!(a)\chi_z$ from $\lambda_a$. (iii) Since $\chi_z$ is $p$-cocartesian, [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] at the test objects $w$ and $v$ gives homotopy pullbacks $\operatorname{Map}_E(h_!z,-)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_E(z,-)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_B(b,b'')}\operatorname{Map}_B(b',b'')$, and since $p(c)=\mathrm{id}_{b''}$ the map $c_*$ lies over the identity of $\operatorname{Map}_B(b',b'')\to\operatorname{Map}_B(b,b'')$. Pasting ([lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting]) these two homotopy pullbacks shows the square formed by $c_*$ and $\chi_z^*$ is a homotopy pullback, which is (ii). This is where the constant-arrow condition defining $A_p$ is used: for an arbitrary arrow $c$ of $E$ the argument fails. Every object $a$ over every edge $u$ of $E$ has such a $\sigma$, so $t$ is a cocartesian fibration.

source.place: Proposition 7.7, proof that target evaluation is cocartesian.

proof.text: Under the fibre description of step 3, $\sigma$ sends $a:z\to x$ to $\bar u\circ h_!(a):h_!z\to y$, so transport for $t$ is the displayed formula. The projection $\mathrm{pr}_1:E\times_BE\to E$ is the degreewise pullback of $p$ along $p$; by the horn definition in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] an edge $(u,e)$ is $\mathrm{pr}_1$-cocartesian when $e$ is $p$-cocartesian (a $\Lambda^n_0$-problem for $\mathrm{pr}_1$ is the same as one for $p$ on the second factor), and such lifts exist, so $\mathrm{pr}_1$ is a cocartesian fibration. $(t,s)$ sends $\sigma$ to $(u,\chi_z)$, which is $\mathrm{pr}_1$-cocartesian. Any other $t$-cocartesian edge with source $a$ over $u$ is $\sigma$ followed by an equivalence in the fibre $t^{-1}(y)$, whose source component is an equivalence of $E_{b'}$; so its source component is $\chi_z$ followed by an equivalence and is again $p$-cocartesian (composition of cocartesian edges, [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] with $K=\Delta^0$). Hence $(t,s)$ preserves cocartesian edges over $E$.

All constructions above are made by degreewise pullbacks of coherent functor simplicial sets. Applying them to K x Delta^n for an arbitrary simplicial parameter K gives the same factorization, pasting and mapping-space pullback in every degree; the identity and composition simplices are retained because cocartesian transport and composition are coherent in the straightening. Pulling the entire construction back along B' -> B proves naturality under base change. A functor of cocartesian fibrations preserving cocartesian edges carries chi, h_!, bar u and the pasted square to the corresponding data, proving the asserted naturality for such functors. No colimit is used.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q02-488daeb1f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item and verified the statement myself: Shah's thesis is not in literature/, so the proof is agent-written. The statement is true. The key point is that t is cocartesian over every edge u of E, not only over p-cocartesian edges, because every test object c of A_p lies over an identity of B. I checked the small cases B=Δ⁰ (classical ev_1, fibre E_{/x}), an identity edge, empty E and p=id. The fibre, the transport formula ū∘h_!(a), and preservation of cocartesian edges by (t,s) into E×_B E are all correct. Three repairable faults, all fixed in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-six-functors/lem-coef-fiberwise-arrow-target-cocartesian.json with the statement unchanged. (a) Step 2 said n-simplices of A_p lie in a single fibre, which is false for n≥1, and it asserted that A_p→B is cocartesian without proof; it is rewritten through lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport with K=Δ¹ and the pullback along c. (b) Step 5 computed mapping spaces in Arr(E), never reduced Map_{A_p} to them, and never used p(c)=id; it is rewritten with lem-coef-infinity-edge-pullback-mapping-fiber (3) for K=Δ¹, arrow-morphism-square, lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion and lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting. (c) Step 1 used the wrong inclusion ({1}→Δ¹ where ∅→Δ¹ is needed) and never showed t is an inner fibration; t is now the pullback of the {1}→Δ¹ corner isofibration along (id,cp). Step 6 now proves that pr_1:E×_B E→E is cocartesian and that every t-cocartesian edge is preserved. Step 4 now cites the p_{Δ¹}-cocartesian square it uses. The four added proof_deps are split nodes of unit sk-prop-sf-biduality-general, so no tool_uses are needed; the dependency closure (734 nodes) does not contain the item, so there is no cycle.
